title: Bisteeki Digaag
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Chicken breast in a lemon, garlic and olive oil marinade, seared a minute a side, with a quick pan sauce of butter, onion, hot stock and balsamic poured over — the dish for guests who arrive without warning.
longDesc: Somali hospitality does not allow for saying you have nothing in. This is the answer to an unannounced visit: a marinade mixed in the time it takes the pan to heat, a minute a side on the chicken, and a sauce built in the same pan while the meat rests. Households that take this seriously keep frozen suugo in reserve for the same reason.
ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) boneless chicken breast, sliced thin
1 tbsp vegetable seasoning, or 2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 yellow or red bell pepper, sliced
steps: Mix the olive oil, minced garlic, vegetable seasoning, lemon juice and black pepper in a bowl.
Turn the chicken through the marinade in the same bowl, coating both sides, and leave it 20 minutes.
Heat a pan over medium-high and cook the chicken for no more than a minute a side.
Lift the chicken onto a warm plate. In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the minced onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Pour in the hot stock — it must be hot, or it drops the pan temperature and the sauce stalls.
Add the balsamic vinegar, then the sliced bell pepper and the cilantro, and cook for barely a minute.
Finish with black pepper, spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve.
chefTips: A minute a side, no more. Chicken breast this thin is done almost on contact and dries out immediately afterwards.
Warm the stock before it goes in. Cold liquid into a hot pan stops everything and you lose the fond.
Slice the breast thin and even. Thick pieces cannot cook in the time the recipe allows.
Everything after the chicken comes out happens in the same pan, in about two minutes. Have the stock hot and the vegetables cut before you start.
commonMistakes: Cooking the chicken through to be certain, which is the whole way to ruin it.
Adding cold stock, which kills the pan and greys the sauce.
Cooking the bell pepper soft — it is there for crunch and colour.
Marinating for hours. Twenty minutes is enough, and lemon juice left much longer starts to cure the surface of the meat.
reheating: Warm very briefly in a covered pan with a spoon of stock.
healthBenefits: Chicken breast is very lean and high in protein.
Lemon, garlic and olive oil carry the seasoning with little salt.
The vegetables are barely cooked, so they keep their vitamin C.
culturalNote: The unannounced guest is a fixture of Somali life, and so is the expectation that they will be fed properly within twenty minutes of sitting down. A dish like this exists because of that expectation, not in spite of it.
